newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIA NAMES 13 PROFESSIONALS FOR MOROCCO TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIA NAMES 13 PROFESSIONALS FOR MOROCCO TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Olympic champions Nigeria have named
13 foreign-based players as part of a 20-man squad to play in
the King Hassan Cup starting next Tuesday in Rabat.
Hosts Morocco will play Nigeria, Croatia and the Czech
Republic in
the annual tournament.
The occasion will be used by Nigeria, like the other three
countries, to prepare for forthcoming 1998 World Cup qualifying
matches.
"Six of the professionals were in the team that won gold at
the Olympic Games in August (and) five were at the 1994 World
Cup," Austin
Mgbolu, press officer of the Nigeria Football Association (NFA)
said on Wednesday.
Mgbolu said Olympic team coach Willy Bazuaye would train the
squad which was completed by seven players from local clubs.
National coach Amodu Shaibu is currently training the
Shooting Stars, the Nigerian club who carry a 2-1 lead to Cairo
for next Friday's second leg match against Zamalek of
Egypt in the African Clubs of Champions Cup final.
Squad:
Goalkeepers: Joseph Oladosu (Reggiana, Italy), Willy
Okpara (Orlando Pirates, South Africa), Andrew Aikhuomogbe
(Katsina United, Nigeria).
Defenders: Mobi Okparaku (Turnhout, Belgium), Kingsley
Obiekwu (Go Ahead Eagles, Netherlands), Austin Eguavoen
(Sacramento
FC, United States), Ben Iroha (San Jose Clash, United States),
Uche Okafor (Kansas City, United States), Bawa Abdullahi (Julius
Berger, Nigeria), Alhassan Mohammed (Bendel Insurance,
Nigeria).
Midfielders: Wilson Oruma (Lens, France), Garba Lawal (FC
Utrecht, Netherlands), Mutiu Adepoju (Real Sociedad, Spain),
Sunday Okoh (Udoji United, Nigeria).
Strikers: Teslim Fatusi (Servette, Switzerland), Samson
Siasia (Al Hilal, Saudi Arabia), Chukwu Ndukwe (Mamelodi
Sundowns, South Africa), Taiwo Oloyede (Julius Berger, Nigeria),
Lucky Ezomo (Udoji United, Nigeria), Baldwin Bazuaye (Udoji
United, Nigeria)
